governing_thought: The two inventories were built against inclusion criteria declared in advance and recorded through a metadata design whose fields carry controlled value lists, so the counts and distributions they produce can be read as a bounded, checkable picture of Thailand's adaptation data landscape at the scope and status the inventories themselves state.

narrative_scqa.situation: The Department of Climate Change and Environment and the agencies it works with already hold a large body of climate and adaptation data, together with reports, dashboards, tools and applications that deliver that data to users, each accumulated according to its own agency's mandate.
narrative_scqa.complication: These holdings had never been counted or described against a single set of criteria. Each agency described its own holdings in its own terms, so the numbers could not be compared across agencies, and there was no central reference that could state what the country actually holds or in what condition.
narrative_scqa.question: On what criteria and to what standard should the existing adaptation data assets be counted and described, so that the resulting figures form a data landscape picture that can be read and traced back?
narrative_scqa.answer: The consultant defined what each inventory admits through stated criteria, surveyed the holdings by desk research against published sources, and recorded every entry through a metadata design built on recognized reference frameworks with controlled value lists, so that the resulting counts and distributions read as a bounded picture of the national data landscape rather than as an unqualified claim of completeness.

argument_units.claim: The two inventories record two different classes of data asset, and the distinction governs what may be counted in each: the Baseline Data Inventory records the upstream datasets that feed analysis and product development, while the Information Product Inventory records the products and channels through which data is delivered to users.
argument_units.grounds: The Baseline Data Inventory was established to collect the raw datasets necessary for developing adaptation information services that exist and are in use today, each entry recording source, coverage, year, resolution, limitations, and whether the data is Historical or Projected. The Information Product Inventory was established to collect the climate information products and services that exist and are in use today, developed by government agencies, international organizations, and other relevant data providers; the products collected cover analytical reports, data dashboards, APIs, and web applications, with named examples including Risk MAP and T-Plat Info, and each entry records the product owner, developer, and reference data source so that the role each product plays within the adaptation data system is visible. The approved executive-summary text for section 2.4 states the same division in its opening: baseline datasets are the upstream data for analysis, while information products are what takes data to users, with 260 datasets from 44 organizations and 99 products from 45 organizations respectively.
argument_units.warrant: Two inventories counted against a single undifferentiated notion of 'data asset' would double-count the same holding — once as a dataset and again as the dashboard that publishes it — and would make the two totals non-additive. Fixing the asset class per inventory is what makes 260 and 99 meaningful separate figures, and it is also what makes the later observation about missing product-to-dataset lineage a statement about a real relationship rather than a category confusion.
argument_units.application_to_design: The catalog schema keeps the two inventories as separate registers with their own metadata sets (39 fields for baseline datasets, 12 for information products) rather than one merged table, and any future consolidation into the department's central data catalog inherits this two-register structure as the basis for linking a product back to the datasets that feed it.

argument_units.claim: Three stated criteria determine what each inventory admits — one governing the dataset catalog, one governing the product catalog, and one applying to both — and the survey that filled them was conducted as desk research against published sources rather than through submissions from the holding agencies.
argument_units.grounds: The approved executive-summary text for section 2.1 records three inclusion criteria, which are parallel tests rather than ranked stages. The first takes the products and services the department developed itself or participated in developing as the starting point, and this criterion governs the scope of the dataset catalog: the department's own products identify the upstream datasets that must be catalogued. The second covers data products already published at global, regional, and domestic level, including international platforms recognized in climate risk assessment and adaptation planning work, and this criterion governs the scope of the product catalog. The third covers products and datasets held by other agencies whose mandates relate to adaptation, such as water resources management and disaster response, and applies to both inventories. On method, the survey was carried out by searching published and documentary sources combined with interviews with project stakeholders, with details verified against the source material; the collected records may therefore not yet cover every domestic holding. The count of 44 owning organizations in the catalog file is the number of agencies that own the datasets found by this search, not a count of agencies that submitted or confirmed records.
argument_units.warrant: An inventory whose boundary is not stated in advance cannot be audited: a reader has no way to tell whether an absent dataset is genuinely absent from the national landscape or was merely outside an unstated boundary. Stating which criterion governs which inventory converts every later count into a claim about a defined population, and stating that the population was assembled from published sources tells the reader exactly what kind of visibility the figures rest on — what could be found and read, which is not the same as what every agency holds.
argument_units.application_to_design: The three criteria double as the admission test for the central data catalog after handover: a candidate entry is admitted when it satisfies the criterion governing its register, which gives the department a stated rule for adding records rather than requiring a fresh scoping judgment each time.

argument_units.claim: Both inventories are anchored to published reference frameworks rather than to categories invented for this project, with each framework carrying a specific and different job: the government data catalogue standard governs catalog structure, the IPCC risk framework governs how baseline datasets are grouped, ISO 19115 governs spatial metadata, and the global climate services framework together with the national adaptation plan govern how information products are positioned and grouped by sector.
argument_units.grounds: For the Baseline Data Inventory, three reference frameworks are named: the Digital Government Development Agency's Government Data Catalogue Guideline (มสพร. 1-2564) as the basis for metadata structure, standard code lists, and data governance principles; the IPCC risk assessment framework, which defines risk as the interaction of hazard, exposure, and vulnerability, with vulnerability comprising sensitivity and adaptive capacity, used as the backbone for grouping baseline datasets by risk component; and ISO 19115 (Geographic Information — Metadata) as the reference standard for datasets with a spatial dimension, covering spatial extent, coordinate reference system, resolution, and data quality. For the Information Product Inventory, four frameworks are named with stated jobs: มสพร. 1-2564 for catalog structure, particularly the key product attributes of owner, developer, reference data source, and service conditions; the WMO Global Framework for Climate Services (GFCS) for identifying where each product sits in the climate service chain — observation, research and prediction, information systems, or user interface platforms; the IPCC risk framework for linking each product to the risk components it serves; and Thailand's National Adaptation Plan (NAP) for classifying which adaptation sector each product supports, such as water management, agriculture, public health, or human settlements and security. The DGA standard itself specifies 14 mandatory metadata items — data_type, title, owner_org, maintainer, maintainer_email, tag_string, notes, objective, update frequency unit and interval, geo_coverage, data_source, data_format, data_category, license_id — and 9 optional items, which is the field pool the project drew from and extended.
argument_units.warrant: Classification categories invented for a single project expire with it: the next contractor cannot map its own work onto them, and the resulting counts cannot be compared with anything produced elsewhere. Binding each classification axis to a framework that already has standing — a national government standard for catalog structure, an international scientific framework for risk grouping, an international standard for spatial metadata, and the country's own adaptation plan for sector grouping — is what allows a figure from this inventory to be read against other national and international reporting, and what lets a successor extend the catalog without renegotiating its vocabulary.
argument_units.application_to_design: Each framework maps onto a specific part of the catalog schema — DGA fields into the metadata core, IPCC risk components into cdm_sub_domain, ISO 19115 into the spatial and quality field group, GFCS into the product's service-chain position, NAP into the sectors field — so that the schema documents its own provenance and each field can be traced back to the standard that justifies it.

argument_units.claim: The metadata for both inventories was assembled by blending three standards rather than adopting any one wholesale — the national catalogue standard supplies the core, ISO 19115 supplies the grouping structure, and project-specific extensions carry the risk and adaptation dimensions that neither general standard provides.
argument_units.grounds: For the Baseline Data Inventory, the data structure is defined in a Data Dictionary specifying 39 fields in total, merging three standards: ISO 19115 metadata layers as the sub-grouping structure, the DGA (มสพร. 1-2564) metadata list as the metadata core, and project-specific extension metadata to support risk classification under the conceptual data model. For the Information Product Inventory, field groups follow ISO 19115 and reference the DGA standard metadata list for the basic data section, using 12 metadata items in total. The approved executive-summary text for section 2.1 records the same design decision at executive altitude: the metadata framework takes มสพร. 1-2564 as its starting point, selects only the fields that suit the project's context, and adds fields specific to risk and adaptation data, such as the data domain and a temporal dimension separating historical data from future projections. The catalog file confirms both extension fields are populated in practice: cdm_domain and cdm_sub_domain carry the risk classification, and temporal_dimension separates Historical (241 of 260 records), Projected (153), and Forecast (7), with records able to carry more than one value.
argument_units.warrant: A general government catalogue standard is written for datasets of every kind and therefore cannot express whether a dataset describes a hazard or a vulnerability, or whether it looks backward at what happened or forward at what is projected — the two distinctions on which all climate risk work turns. Adopting the standard unchanged would produce records that satisfy government cataloguing policy while remaining unusable for risk analysis; discarding it would produce records unusable to the rest of government. Taking the standard as the core and extending it is what allows these records to be registered as government data assets and queried as risk data at the same time.
argument_units.application_to_design: The 39-field and 12-field dictionaries are published in full as appendices, so that the department can operate the catalog and a successor contractor can implement it against a field-level specification rather than reconstructing the schema from the narrative.

argument_units.claim: Within both dictionaries the fields are split into general and technical metadata by one stated test — what the field enables the user to do — rather than by which standard the field came from.
argument_units.grounds: The rule is stated explicitly for the Baseline Data Inventory: a metadata item whose primary function is to help the user find, understand, trust, or govern a dataset is classified as general metadata, with dataset title, CDM category, related hazards, sectors, and owning agency as the given examples, while a metadata item that affects the ability to access, interpret, link, or technically use the data is classified as technical metadata, with spatial extent, time period, resolution, file format, and access conditions as the given examples. The same division applies to the product inventory's 12 items: general metadata for finding and identifying the product, technical metadata for access and service-type classification, with the stated selection principle that each item must genuinely help the user find, understand, or classify the product. Basic items such as product name, owner, developer, and access link are described as necessary for registering the asset under government data catalogue practice.
argument_units.warrant: Grouping fields by their source standard would scatter functionally related fields across the record and leave the person completing the record with no principle for deciding where a new field belongs. Grouping by what the field lets the user do gives both the person recording a dataset and the future system implementer the same test, so the structure survives the addition of fields neither standard anticipated.
argument_units.application_to_design: The general and technical split is carried into the catalog's field ordering, so that the fields answerable from administrative knowledge of a dataset are separated from those requiring technical inspection of the data itself.

argument_units.claim: The classifying metadata fields take their values from fixed option lists rather than free text, which is what makes the two inventories aggregable at all.
argument_units.grounds: The metadata design assigns controlled option lists to the fields that classify each entry. For the Baseline Data Inventory these include cdm_domain with 4 options classifying a dataset by its time horizon and role in the risk cycle (ADAPTATION_PLANNING, FORWARD-LOOKING, IMPACT_(BACKWARD-LOOKING), SPATIAL_UNIT) and cdm_sub_domain with 10 options classifying by risk component (CLIMATE_DRIVER, COMPOSITE_INDEX, DISASTER_RECORD, EXPOSURE, HAZARD, LOSS_&_DAMAGE, RESPONSE, RISK_METRIC, SPATIAL_UNIT, VULNERABILITY), with further classification by cdm_data_entity and related_hazards; the complete set of 21 option lists is placed in an appendix. For the Information Product Inventory these include service_type with 5 options (Dashboard, Data Catalog, GIS Tool, Policy Document, Report), use_case with 5 options (Knowledge and Capacity Building, Climate Data, Forecasting and Prediction, Risk and Impact Assessment, Decision and Policy Support), delivery_format (Web Platform, Mobile App, API), geo_coverage (Global, Regional, Thailand), and NAP sectors. The catalog file demonstrates the constraint holds in the recorded data: across all 260 records, cdm_sub_domain takes exactly the 10 documented values and cdm_domain exactly the 4, with no free-text variants.
argument_units.warrant: Free-text values cannot be aggregated: two records describing the same kind of dataset in different words produce entries that no query can group, which would leave the inventory unable to answer the distribution questions it exists to answer. Fixing the permissible values per field is therefore not a formatting preference but the precondition for every count and percentage reported later in this section, each of which is produced by grouping records on exactly these fields.
argument_units.application_to_design: The option lists are carried into the catalog as controlled vocabularies with the full lists held in the appendices, which is what makes the distribution analysis reproducible directly from the catalog file rather than dependent on manual recoding.

argument_units.claim: Baseline datasets cluster on the input side of the risk equation and thin out sharply toward its outcome side, and the same asymmetry appears again on the time axis, where the inventory is dominated by forward-looking data and holds comparatively little that records what has already occurred.
argument_units.grounds: All 260 baseline records stand at Baseline-Draft endorsement status and Unverified-Baseline validation status, without exception, and the figures below are therefore an opening picture awaiting confirmation from the owning agencies. Computed directly from the catalog file across all 260 records, the distribution by risk component is: vulnerability 72 records (27.7 per cent), exposure 68 (26.2 per cent), climate driver 49 (18.8 per cent), hazard 36 (13.8 per cent), loss and damage 11 (4.2 per cent), composite index 10 (3.8 per cent), risk metric 5 (1.9 per cent), response 4 (1.5 per cent), spatial unit 3 (1.2 per cent), and disaster record 2 (0.8 per cent). The four components describing the inputs to a risk assessment — vulnerability, exposure, climate driver, and hazard — together account for 225 of 260 records (86.5 per cent), while loss and damage, risk metric, and response together account for 20 records (7.7 per cent). The distribution by time horizon shows the same shape: FORWARD-LOOKING 224 records (86.2 per cent), IMPACT_(BACKWARD-LOOKING) 25 (9.6 per cent), SPATIAL_UNIT 7 (2.7 per cent), and ADAPTATION_PLANNING 4 (1.5 per cent). The approved executive-summary text for section 2.4 reports the same risk-component figures and the same 86.5 per cent grouping.
argument_units.warrant: The risk components are not independent categories but stages of one chain: hazard, exposure, and vulnerability are what a risk assessment consumes, while risk metrics, loss and damage, and response records are what it produces and what allows a later assessment to be checked against what actually happened. A distribution weighted 86.5 per cent toward the input stages therefore describes an inventory equipped to run assessments forward while holding little of the record that closes the loop — and the near-identical split on the time axis, 86.2 per cent forward-looking against 9.6 per cent backward-looking, shows the same shape confirmed independently by a different field.
argument_units.application_to_design: The risk-component and time-horizon fields are retained as primary reporting axes of the catalog so that this distribution can be recomputed as the inventory grows, giving the department a standing measure of how the balance shifts as new datasets are registered and confirmed.

argument_units.claim: Across adaptation sectors the baseline inventory is led by datasets that serve more than one sector at once, and on the time axis most records carry a historical series while a smaller majority also carry projections.
argument_units.grounds: Computed from the catalog file across all 260 records, where a record may carry more than one sector value and percentages are therefore taken against the 260-record base rather than summing to 100: cross-cutting 116 records (44.6 per cent), human settlements and security 80 (30.8 per cent), water resources management 55 (21.2 per cent), agriculture and food security 36 (13.8 per cent), tourism 28 (10.8 per cent), public health 25 (9.6 per cent), and natural resources management 19 (7.3 per cent). On the temporal dimension field, likewise multi-valued: Historical 241 records (92.7 per cent), Projected 153 (58.8 per cent), Forecast 7 (2.7 per cent).
argument_units.warrant: A dataset tagged to several sectors is one that more than one adaptation mandate can draw on, so a cross-cutting share of 44.6 per cent means the inventory's largest single group is shared infrastructure rather than sector-specific holdings — which is what makes a single central catalog worth operating instead of separate sector registers. On the time axis, the 92.7 per cent carrying historical series against 58.8 per cent carrying projections means most datasets can support trend analysis and a clear majority can also support forward scenario work, with the two overlapping on the same records.
argument_units.application_to_design: Sector and temporal dimension are kept as multi-valued fields rather than single-select, since forcing one sector per dataset would have suppressed the cross-cutting group that turns out to be the inventory's largest, and would have hidden the overlap between historical and projected coverage on the same record.

argument_units.claim: Access conditions are the characteristic that most determines whether a listed dataset can actually be used, and the great majority of the baseline inventory is restricted, reachable only by request to the owning agency.
argument_units.grounds: Computed from the catalog file across all 260 records: restricted 214 records, public 43, and 3 records with no access condition stated. Taken against the 257 records that state an access condition, the split is 83.3 per cent restricted to 16.7 per cent public. On file format, 152 records (58.5 per cent) include CSV, counting records where CSV appears together with other formats; the remaining recorded format values are Vector (44), other-specified (34), Raster (25), Unknown (25), Database (14), PDF (14), and Image (9), with records able to carry more than one format. The approved executive-summary text for section 2.4 states the same figures on the same 257-record base and draws the same reading, that use of most datasets depends on the request and authorization procedure of the owning agency.
argument_units.warrant: A restricted dataset is present in the inventory but absent from any workflow that has to run on a schedule: each use requires a request and a wait, which rules out automated linking and repeated analysis regardless of how well the dataset is described. The count of 260 therefore describes what exists, while the 43 public records describe what is available without negotiation — two different quantities that a single figure would conflate.
argument_units.application_to_design: Access rights are recorded per record and separately from metadata access rights, so that the catalog can be published and searched in full while distinguishing the entries a user can retrieve directly from those requiring a request, and so that the department can track the restricted share as data-sharing agreements are put in place.

argument_units.claim: The information product inventory shows delivery concentrated almost entirely on the web and content concentrated on cross-sector products, with mobile and programmatic access barely present.
argument_units.grounds: From the 99 products collected: by geographic scope, national 62 products (62.6 per cent), global 31 (31.3 per cent), and regional 6 (6.1 per cent); by delivery channel, web platform 92 (92.9 per cent), mobile application 5 (5.1 per cent), and API 2 (2.0 per cent); and by adaptation sector, cross-cutting 58 products (58.6 per cent), with sector-specific services such as human settlements, agriculture, and public health comparatively few. Dashboards and geographic information tools are the dominant content types, and use cases concentrate on climate data access and risk assessment. The dissemination presentation of the study results reports the product-type distribution as risk assessment 32 per cent, weather and environmental monitoring data 30 per cent, climate information systems and models 22 per cent, impact analysis 18 per cent, decision support platforms 15 per cent, and sector-specific climate information services 13 per cent, where one product may be classified under more than one type and the percentages therefore cannot be summed across types. The approved executive-summary text for section 2.4 carries these same figures and states the same overlap qualification.
argument_units.warrant: Delivery channel determines who can build on a product: a web platform serves a person reading a page, while an API is what allows another system to consume the same information automatically. With 92 of 99 products delivered as web platforms and 2 as APIs, the existing products are built for direct reading rather than for reuse by other systems, which bears directly on what a future national platform can integrate as against what it would have to rebuild.
argument_units.application_to_design: Delivery format, geographic coverage, service type, and use case are retained as classification axes of the product register, so that the integration options for any candidate product can be read off the catalog when the national platform's build sequence is planned.

argument_units.claim: Read together, the two inventories describe a landscape whose assets are held in many hands and described in each holder's own terms, with no recorded lineage connecting a published product back to the datasets it draws on.
argument_units.grounds: Computed from the catalog file, the 260 baseline datasets are held by 44 owning organizations, with the three largest holdings at the Thai Meteorological Department 37 records (14.2 per cent), the Department of Climate Change and Environment 26 (10.0 per cent), and the Geo-Informatics and Space Technology Development Agency 17 (6.5 per cent) — together 80 records, 30.8 per cent of the inventory, leaving the remaining 180 records spread across 41 agencies. The parallel figure for products is 99 products across 45 owning agencies, an average of about 2 products per agency. Read across both inventories, products and baseline datasets alike are developed and held by many agencies in dispersed fashion, and the lineage between a product and its source datasets is not recorded anywhere in either register.
argument_units.warrant: Dispersion across 44 and 45 agencies reflects that adaptation data is generated where each agency's mandate generates it. What follows from it is a specific consequence: when a product's source datasets are recorded nowhere, a correction to a dataset cannot be traced forward to the products that carry it, and a figure appearing in a product cannot be traced back to what produced it. The two inventories give the country its first common description of these holdings, and the lineage link is the piece that description does not yet carry.
argument_units.application_to_design: The conceptual data model is carried as the shared classification structure across both registers precisely so that products and datasets are described in one vocabulary, which is the precondition for recording product-to-dataset lineage as the central catalog is populated in the next phase.
